items.title: Arnold Loyacano Interview, 1956-09-29
items.q: George Brunus was in that band and Pansy Lane, Jack's son, and myself.

ctx.x: Oh, yeah. George Brunus was in that band and Pansy Lane, Jack's son, and myself. I don't know just who else. But you see... About how old were you then? Oh, I was about 14. Jack lived on Port Street. And we used to go down there and stay overnight. We'd play a job Saturday night and stay at his house. And then we'd catch the Smokey Mary on a Sunday morning and go out and play at Millenburg. When you were kids at it?
Yeah, sure. Did you get paid?

items.title: Georg Brunis Interview, 1958-06-03
items.q: then we replaced Arnold Lake Canna with Steve Brown

ctx.x: Uh, was, uh, Mike Fritzel, the, uh, boss, uh? Yeah, that's right, that's right. You don't have to lean over close to the dingus. No. You don't have to talk right at that, that'll take a moment.

We replaced, uh, Frank Snyder with Ben Pollack, and we replaced Elmer Schoble with Mel Stitzel on piano, then we replaced Arnold Lake Canna with Steve Brown, who to me was the world's greatest jazz bass player. In fact, he started all these guys slapping a bass. No. And I think he's now Secretary of the Union in Detroit.
